images.title: Nobody at reception
images.alt: An empty company reception desk faces rows of waiting chairs, with a researcher's yellow coat left on one seat.
images.caption: A proposed company reception area explores absence through a familiar waiting-room layout. The abandoned coat offers a possible story detail without deciding who left it or why.
images.question: Which everyday sign of occupation would make an empty room feel most recently abandoned?
images.scene: Empty company reception lobby deep in the Backrooms. Symmetrical low eye-level composition, rows of faded green vinyl waiting chairs facing a frosted-glass reception hatch with nobody behind it. A practical yellow work coat lies neatly over one near chair; a warm paper cup and an unlit desk telephone behind glass suggest a recent departure. Cracked linoleum, drooping houseplant, blank paperwork slot, cool greenish fluorescent ceiling. The far doorway is an ordinary narrow yellow corridor. No people, no visible sphere, no monsters, no signs or readable text. Quiet institutional neglect and expectation.

images.title: The landing between layers
images.alt: A yellow-suited researcher climbs a concrete service stairwell where rusted pipes give way to office partitions.
images.caption: This proposed transition compresses utility infrastructure and office materials into one stairwell. The changing surfaces suggest the collapsed region's history without changing the established excavation order.
images.question: Which material should players recognize first when one architectural layer intrudes into another?
images.scene: Tall-feeling service stairwell composed within landscape 3:2, camera high above looking down a rectangular stair void. A lone yellow-suited researcher climbing concrete stairs with a small work lamp. Upper landing has ordinary beige office partitions and hanging acoustic ceiling tiles; lower landing has dense rusted pipework and old valves. The transitions are compressed and bent around the stair core, quietly impossible but readable. Practical guardrails, stained concrete, dusty fluorescent light, green-gray and beige palette. No giant sphere visible, no flesh, no sweeping exterior vista. Focus on vertical circulation and contrasting ordinary materials.

images.title: Catch what the shell gives back
images.alt: Researchers use a hammer and a supported mesh tray to collect glass fragments from a small excavation patch.
images.caption: A catch tray proposes a practical way to make the established hammer-and-glass loop visible. Fragment behavior, collection assistance and the equipment required remain open.
images.question: What makes collecting shattered glass satisfying without turning every fragment into busywork?
images.scene: Close side-on action study at the reflective glass exterior excavation face. Crop the enormous curved shell tightly as a silver wall, not a full sphere. Two researchers in yellow suits on braced scaffold: one has just struck a small prefractured patch with a plain heavy hammer; the other steadies a supported rigid metal-mesh catching tray directly below. A modest cascade of small mirror shards falls into it, frozen in work-light highlights. Glass reflects yellow ceiling panels and railings. Believable arms and grips, restrained debris, no explosions, no later layers or flesh visible. Focus on collection choreography and tactile brittle fracture.

images.title: Listen before turning
images.alt: A researcher holds a contact microphone against a valve bank while a teammate watches a portable analog meter.
images.caption: A proposed investigation setup treats the Utility Halls as something to listen to as well as excavate. The relationship between pipe resonance, clues and any puzzle is still undecided.
images.question: How could a sound-based clue remain understandable to players who need a visual alternative?
images.scene: Intimate equipment-focused scene in a low Utility Halls alcove. Parallel copper and steel pipes terminate in a small bank of differently sized mechanical valves. One yellow-gloved researcher holds a wired contact microphone firmly against a pipe; another watches a rugged portable analog meter on a folding stool. Cable clearly connects microphone and meter, no readable dial labels. Condensation beads, flaking paint, pipe clamps, restrained warm task lamp in green fluorescent gloom. Instruments mundane and plausible, no holographic sound waves or magical glow. No sphere visible. Deliberate listening and observation, not drilling.

images.title: Water above the tiles
images.alt: A still pool appears on the ceiling of a tiled room, reflecting a researcher standing on the dry floor below.
images.caption: An inverted water surface proposes a spatial anomaly within the Poolrooms. It invites discussion of orientation and readable warning signs without establishing gravity-changing traversal.
images.question: What first tells players that this is water above them rather than a normal reflection?
images.scene: Silent Poolrooms side chamber with a dry white-tile floor and a rectangular shallow swimming pool impossibly held upside down flush against the ceiling. A stainless pool ladder rises from the ceiling's turquoise water and curves downward into the room; its inverted orientation makes the anomaly clear. One yellow-suited researcher stands small on the dry floor looking up, reflected in the overhead water. Soft cyan caustic light plays on tiled pillars, a single suspended droplet emphasizes uncertainty, no deluge. Landscape wide shot with strong ceiling plane, no sphere visible, no core, no floating person, no portal.

images.title: Everything points to one door
images.alt: Loose blank papers form a low stream through empty office cubicles toward a closed door while researchers watch.
images.caption: A proposed directional anomaly uses familiar office debris as a clue. The moving paper could suggest a route or danger, but its cause and gameplay role remain open.
images.question: What would distinguish a helpful directional cue from an anomaly the team should avoid?
images.scene: Low floor-level view through an abandoned office of half-height cubicles, worn carpet and acoustic tiles. Loose BLANK papers skim and curl in a thin stream a few inches above the floor, all drawn toward the narrow gap beneath one plain closed door at the far end. Two yellow-suited researchers pause behind a cubicle edge in middle distance, observing without entering the stream. Ordinary desks and dead beige monitors, subtle dust, stale amber fluorescent light, hints of compressed leaning partitions. No giant vortex, no magical symbols, no sphere visible, no readable writing. Delicate inexplicable movement rather than spectacle.

images.title: Keys without matching rooms
images.alt: An open hotel key cabinet holds mismatched brass keys, with one oversized key laid beside a bent room plan.
images.caption: This Terror Hotel prop study proposes a link between ordinary keys and unreliable room layouts. Key functions, collection rules and any associated puzzle remain exploratory.
images.question: What physical difference could make one key memorable before the team knows where it belongs?
images.scene: Front-three-quarter close still-life of an open battered hotel service key cabinet at a dim concierge counter. Rows of differently shaped old brass keys hang on simple hooks with blank tags, several conspicuously empty hooks. One unusually long but practical brass key lies beside a folded floor plan containing only unlabeled geometric room outlines, an old mechanical bell and a yellow researcher's glove. Worn burgundy felt backing, tarnished brass and scratched dark wood, amber shaded lamp. No readable numbers or writing, no occult symbols, no sphere, no people beyond one gloved hand at edge. Rich material study, no fantasy ornate weapons.

images.title: The pattern stops repeating
images.alt: A researcher examines faded wallpaper whose repeating pattern bends out of alignment along a thin adhesive seam.
images.caption: A close Threshold study proposes a visual clue within the final wallpaper covering. Pattern misalignment might guide inspection, but it does not yet define a hidden route or solvent rule.
images.question: How subtle can a wallpaper inconsistency be while still feeling fair to notice?
images.scene: Extreme close material study of faded yellow patterned wallpaper wrapping a gently curved Threshold surface. Normal repeating small floral diamonds abruptly become offset along one narrow vertical adhesive seam, as if two spatial grids disagree. Yellow-gloved hands hold a simple folding ruler and a raking flashlight near the seam without peeling or applying solvent. Fine paper fibers, dust, tiny dry adhesive beads, restrained warm light revealing slight relief. No flesh exposed, no full sphere, no wide chamber, no glowing symbols, no writing. Strong tactile detail and a clear but modest mismatch in decorative repeat.
